title: Service Registry Schema Migration and Alerting Runbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This runbook describes the safe process for performing schema migrations to the platform service registry (metadata-api), together with the observability and alerting changes required to detect regressions early. It covers preflight checks, staged migration steps, live verification, alert thresholds and rollback procedures. Apply this runbook for any production-impacting schema or API contract changes to avoid service discovery and routing regressions.

Scope:
- Applies to the central service-registry (metadata-api) and any read replicas used by routing services such as edge-router, request-router and model-router.
- Covers Postgres schema changes, API surface (v1/v2), and telemetry emitted by the registry.
- Excludes purely client-side SDK changes that do not modify API or DB behavior.

Owners and escalation:
- Primary owner: platform-infra team (pager: @platform-infra-oncall).
- Secondary owner: data-platform (DB migrations).
- Product owner for breaking API changes: API Platform.
- Escalation: oncall -> platform-sre -> infra-eng lead -> VP Eng.

Contact matrix (weekday / after hours):
- platform-infra rotation: +1-555-0101 and slack #platform-oncall
- data-platform lead: Diego Alvarez (diego@redwood.ai)
- API Platform product: Priya Nair (priya@redwood.ai)

Preflight checklist (required):
1) ADR & design review: publish an ADR under decision-records with schema diff and rollout plan.
2) Staging rehearsal: run the exact migration in a staging cluster that mirrors production (replicas and caches).
3) Dry-run: prepare a dry-run using database planning tooling and validate affected row counts.
4) Feature gate: add a feature flag in metadata-api to toggle new schema behavior on/off.
5) Backups: take logical pg_dump and physical base backups; verify restore steps in staging.
6) Canary mirror: configure traffic mirroring for a small percentage of production traffic.
7) Dashboards: create/adjust migration-specific dashboard panels and temporary alert labels.
8) Communicate: publish maintenance window and update the public status page.

Required artifacts (attach to migration ticket):
- SQL migration file and companion rollforward/rollback scripts.
- Migration plan with timed steps and named owners.
- Dashboard diffs and temporary alert configuration.

Monitoring and dashboards (create or update):
- Dashboard title: Service Registry Health - Migration. Include panels for:
  - API 5xx rate for metadata-api (per instance).
  - API latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for metadata-api.
  - Client-side service discovery errors observed by edge-router and request-router.
  - Postgres replication lag for read replicas.
  - Registry cache hit ratio (hits / total lookups).

Alert thresholds (temporary migration adjustments):
- SEV1: metadata-api 5xx rate > 1% sustained for 3 minutes OR absolute 5xx > 50 per minute.
- SEV1: replication lag on any replica > 2 seconds for 5 minutes.
- SEV2: p95 latency > baseline + 200 ms for 10 minutes.
- SEV2: client service-discovery error rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes.
- SEV3: cache hit ratio below 70% for 15 minutes.
Note: mark non-critical alerts with a temporary label migration=true to reduce noise, but do NOT silence SEV1/SEV2 alerts.

Runtime windows and risk profile:
- Preferred times: Sunday 02:00-06:00 UTC or Wednesday 03:00-05:00 UTC.
- Risk levels: low if canary is healthy; medium if migration requires long backfills.
- If any shard requires maintenance > 30 seconds, schedule explicit maintenance window and notify platform customers.

Staged migration procedure (summary):
1) Pre-migration (T-60 to T0): confirm backups, ensure no long-running transactions, set feature flag to false, deploy telemetry that emits migration version tag.
2) Canary (T0 to T+30m): run migration against a canary DB or isolated schema copy; mirror 10% of traffic to the canary; validate 200 responses and success rate >= 99.5% for 30 minutes; verify row counts.
3) Progressive rollout (T+30m to T+3h): if canary healthy, increase mirror to 25% then 50%, toggle feature flag for a subset of internal consumers, and run backfills at low QPS with checkpointing.
4) Full cutover (T+3h): apply migration to primary DB, switch read replicas, remove mirror and increase traffic to 100%, then observe for 60 minutes.
5) Post-migration (T+3h to T+24h): run integration smoke tests for edge-router, request-router and model-router; remove temporary alert labels; document deviations.

Live validation checks and smoke tests (examples):
- API health endpoint should return OK for metadata-api.
- Service count sanity: compare current service row counts against pre-migration snapshot; accept variance <= 2%.
- Cache behavior: spot-check lookup responses for cache-hit header and expect > 80% hit for common keys.

Rollback plan (triggered on SEV1 or unrecoverable regression):
Immediate containment:
- Pause metadata-api traffic by updating routing weight to 0 and fallback to legacy metadata-api.
- Flip feature flag to disable new schema behavior.
- If required, restore DB from pre-migration backup following documented recovery steps (target SLA: 60 minutes).
Post-containment:
- Collect logs and metrics from metadata-api, edge-router and DB.
- Open incident ticket and notify stakeholders.
- Rehearse rollback in staging and update runbook with lessons learned.

Backfill guidance and long job rules:
- Use registry-backfill worker which checkpoints progress in a migration_progress table. Always start with resume-capable runs.
- Constrain concurrency: begin with two workers and increase only if CPU < 60% and DB I/O latency < 10ms.
- Expected throughput target: >= 5,000 rows/min for low-risk changes; document deviation reasons.

Automation snippets (illustrative commands):
- Perform a dry-run plan using Postgres tooling and validate affected row counts in staging.
- Create a traffic mirror rule in edge-router to send a fraction of requests to the canary instance.
- Toggle the feature flag via internal feature flag API to enable or disable new-schema behavior for targeted consumers.

Post-incident and retrospective actions (mandatory for SEV1/SEV2):
- File an incident review under eng-platform/retrospectives within 48 hours.
- Add regression tests to the integration suite covering the issue.
- Update this runbook with explicit timing and missing preflight items.

Appendix: simple SQL migration example (conceptual):
- Begin transaction, add new jsonb column tags with default [], populate tags from legacy columns where present, commit.
- Always include a one-row sanity check after commit to assert schema visibility.

References and related playbooks:
- Service lifecycle orchestration guidelines: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/service-lifecycle-orchestration-guidelines-2026
- Fault isolation and fallback runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/service-dependency-fault-isolation-and-fallback-runbook-2025
- Platform alerting standards: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/platform-alert-routing-and-escalation-playbook-2026

Revision history:
- 2025-09-10: Created by Maya Chen (initial draft).
- 2025-11-21: Added canary mirror commands and backfill guidance (reviewed by Diego Alvarez).
- 2026-02-15: Finalized alert thresholds and dashboard ids; published.

End of runbook.
